failures.text: How does an idea get from a draft all the way to paper trading with real allocated capital?
failures.answer: Sir, an idea climbs a fixed staircase. First it is noted on a nightly card, then drafted once a fixed count how often it fires, and registered only when you say yes, with the study written down before it runs. It is then tested on 2000-2023 at the strict pass mark and run as a paper shadow trial of 20 recorded sessions. It is admitted only if it beats chance and the average stock on 10 separate sessions after costs, passes the leak check and gets your yes; only then may the allocated paper capital use it, and real money needs the final real-money gate and your yes as well. Today nothing has reached that step: the stock rules are 15 of 20 practice sessions of the 20 needed in (best 7 of the 10 winning days needed) and the options line is 11 of 20. One thing that isn't right, sir: explorer: a scan of all 10 coins every 15 minutes ran with an error at 10 Nov 19:45 Toronto. Ask me what's wrong for the details.

problems.why: It uses unexplained internal terms such as 'staircase', 'strict pass mark', 'leak check', 'shadow trial' and 'final real-money gate' that a beginner would not follow.
A single process question gets a dense answer of about 8 long sentences, padded with an unrelated status report on explorer and today's counts.

The garbled phrases 'drafted once a fixed count how often it fires' and 'of the 20 needed in (best 7 of the 10 winning days needed)' do not read as a clear explanation of how an idea moves from draft to allocated capital.

Nifty closed 25,045 (+0.2%) and Bank Nifty 59,741 (+1.5%); foreign institutions bought ₹7,212 crore. the options line passed on Nifty and went short Bank Nifty at 09:15, which that day's rise went against. Portfolio: no change; the managed book holds its three replacements (Eternal, Ajanta Pharma, Cipla). Wednesday 11 Nov, the options line plans no Nifty trade and a Bank Nifty long, with GIFT Nifty pointing about 1.1% higher.

results.text: Is the Indian market open now or closed? When does it open next?
results.answer: Sir, the Indian market is closed now: it is Sunday 1 Nov, 22:30 in India, a weekend with no NSE session. It opens next on Monday 2 Nov, with the pre-open at 09:00 IST and normal trading from 09:15 IST, which is 10:45 pm tonight in Toronto. It closes at 15:30 IST, which is 5:00 am Monday in Toronto. The last session was Friday 30 Oct, when the Nifty closed at 23,053.

results.text: Ananta, how is the relative strength trial going?
results.answer: Sir, the relative-strength trial is on session 5 of 20, expected to finish around 27 Nov. So far its picks did -2.07% against the average liquid stock after costs, and random picks did -1.61%, so the picks are slightly behind random. In testing over 2000-2023 the idea earned about +1.6% to +2.1% over 20 sessions but narrowly missed the strict pass mark. Five sessions is far too early to read anything into it, and nothing trades from it.

results.text: Ananta, what big events are coming up that could move the market?
results.answer: Sir, the nearest big one is India's October inflation (CPI) on Thursday 12 Nov at 16:00 IST, after the close, so the first session that can trade it is Friday 13 Nov. Next come India's GDP for July-September on Monday 30 Nov, and the RBI rate decision on Friday 4 Dec at about 10:00 IST, which can move that session. US inflation for October came out last night, and today is the first Indian session that can trade it. Company results are also due: Tata Power today and Vodafone Idea on Thursday 12 Nov, from your holdings.

results.text: Ananta, how is the book doing?
results.answer: Which book do you mean, sir? 1. the practice book (the research trades). 2. my account on paper (the managed book). 3. the index options line.

results.text: Ananta, when do you ask me which one I mean?
results.answer: Sir, I ask only when a wrong guess would cost something: which draft to approve or skip, which book you mean, or what to flag when nothing came before. For a plain fact question I just answer, and if your voice message is garbled I ask one short question with 2-4 choices. It is one round only: once you pick a choice, that pick is the answer. In the last 7 days I asked 2 times, both about which book you meant, and you picked a choice both times.

results.text: Ananta, how will the market open?
results.answer: Sir, pre-open read at 09:09 IST, before the 09:15 open: Nifty indicated near 25,337 (+1.2% on yesterday's close); Bank Nifty indicated near 60,465 (+1.2% on yesterday's close). These are pre-open matched prices, an indication of the gap; the 09:15 open can differ, and nothing trades on them. Against the 08:30 morning view: The pre-open (Nifty +1.2%, Bank Nifty +1.2%) agrees with what GIFT Nifty showed at 08:30 (+1.1%): the view stands. Nifty would open near 25,337, already above the line that makes it an up day (25,120). A gap of 1% or more: the first 15 to 30 minutes show whether it holds or fills; the managed book skips any buy that opens more than 2% up. Options line: Nifty is indicated +1.2% (up): for that open the plan says no trade. Options line: Bank Nifty is indicated +1.2% (up): for that open the plan says a long (a call option, one lot), closing at the next session's open.

results.text: Ananta, what will the options line do at the open?
results.answer: Sir, the options line's plan for the 09:15 open (written 07:31 IST, on paper, one lot): Nifty: no trade at the open, whichever way it opens. Bank Nifty: a long (a call option, one lot), closing at the next session's open, whichever way it opens. It looks again at 09:30, 09:45 and 10:15 from the first hour's bars, so a pass at the open is not a pass for the day. It was planned with the trend up, the fear gauge high, the US down overnight (the Nasdaq -0.7% on Tue 10 Nov), foreign investors' futures positioning low, no scheduled event. No input was stale. For the open as it is indicated now: Nifty is indicated +1.2% (up): for that open the plan says no trade. Bank Nifty is indicated +1.2% (up): for that open the plan says a long (a call option, one lot), closing at the next session's open.
